glossary.canonical: KS

glossary.canonical: usbvideo (usbvideo.sys)

glossary.note: REPORT defines it inside the WinUSB term. README section heading 'Windows, normal camera driver (usbvideo.sys)' is fine as the first use.

glossary.concept: Generic USB driver and the driver swap
glossary.canonical: WinUSB; 'driver swap' = rebinding a camera from usbvideo to WinUSB
glossary.first_use_form: WinUSB (Microsoft's generic USB driver; the 'driver swap' replaces usbvideo with it so libusb can stream)
glossary.note: 'WinUSB phase 3' and 'phase 2' are study phases, not rig phases. See the 'phase' entry.

glossary.canonical: alt setting (alt)
glossary.first_use_form: alt setting ('alt'): one of the fixed isochronous slot sizes a camera offers
glossary.note: REPORT defines it. README G5 says 'isochronous allocation (alt setting)', which is consistent.

glossary.canonical: PTS, SCR (STC + SOF), SOF, QPC
glossary.first_use_form: PTS/SCR (UVC payload-header timestamps on the camera clock; SCR pairs the camera's STC with the USB SOF frame counter); QPC (Windows host clock)
glossary.note: REPORT defines PTS, SCR, SOF and QPC but not STC. Define STC = source time clock (the camera clock inside SCR). Note that SOF means both the camera's reported SOF counter (broken on the C922, 884/s) and the host/ESP32-S3 USB frame clock.

glossary.concept: Mapping camera time to host time
glossary.canonical: SCR→QPC mapping (via the xHCI frame-number→QPC IOCTL)
glossary.first_use_form: SCR→QPC mapping (xHCI frame-number→QPC IOCTL; exact only ~2–3.5 s, REPORT finding 14)
glossary.note: README line 50 says 'SOF→QPC'. The plan, REPORT finding 13 and DESIGN say 'SCR→QPC'.

glossary.canonical: flash method (monitor-flash ground truth)
glossary.first_use_form: the flash method (monitor-flash ground truth, timing/VERIFY_method.md)
glossary.note: Only DESIGN defines GT. Elsewhere spell out 'ground truth'. rocsync_review alone says 'screen-flash'.

glossary.canonical: flash floor (~0.5 ms, measured) vs rig floor (est. 10–20 µs strobe, 15–30 µs bar)
glossary.first_use_form: flash floor (~0.5 ms: the limit of the monitor-flash ground truth, so true error ≤ that)
glossary.note: 'Ground-truth floor' means 0.5 ms in REPORT finding 15 but the rig's 10–30 µs estimate in sync_rig/README line 10. Always qualify floor with 'flash' or 'rig'.

glossary.canonical: ESP32 sync rig (sync_rig/), 'the rig' after first use
variants_seen: ESP32 timing and sync test rig

Only the MJPEG-matrix cells used the DS filter.
